stem: A client with prediabetes and overweight asks how to reduce the risk of progressing to type 2 diabetes. Which plan best reflects the CDC National Diabetes Prevention Program evidence base?

options.A: Eliminate essentially all carbohydrate foods and avoid structured physical activity until weight normalizes.
options.B: Work toward about 5%–7% weight loss through healthier eating and at least 150 minutes of physical activity each week.
options.C: Rely on vigorous exercise alone without changing eating patterns or body weight.
options.D: Wait to make lifestyle changes until blood glucose reaches the diabetes range.

rationale: CDC's National Diabetes Prevention Program is based on evidence that people with prediabetes can reduce progression to type 2 diabetes through structured lifestyle change, including healthier eating, modest weight loss of about 5%–7% of body weight, and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week. B directly reflects those evidence-based targets. A promotes an extreme diet and defers activity; C omits the combined lifestyle approach; D delays prevention until after progression.
educational_objective: Teach clients with prediabetes that modest weight loss achieved through healthier eating plus regular physical activity is an evidence-based strategy to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes.

audit_findings: CDC directly supports the 5%–7% weight-loss and ≥150-min/week activity targets, so the numeric precision is supported rather than inferred. B uniquely reflects the combined evidence-based program; A/C/D are realistic misconceptions but clearly wrong. No medication or universal diet prescription is added.
